title: Before every move
line: Ask what the other side's last move attacks, then answer it: move, guard or capture.

steps.text: Before every move, ask what the other side's last move attacks. Here White's pawn has just stepped up, and it attacks your knight.
The first answer: move the attacked piece. Bring your knight back to a square where nothing can take it.

wrong.e4c5: Nothing takes it there, but the pawn steps up once more and chases it again. Go back to safety.
wrong.e4d2: A white piece takes it there.
wrong.e4f2: That takes a pawn, but the king takes the knight.

steps.hint: Go back the way the knight came.
steps.after: The knight is safe on the square it came from.

steps.text: Another game. You are White, and Black's knight has just come out. Tap the white piece or pawn it attacks.
steps.hint: A knight jumps two squares one way and one the other.
steps.after: The knight attacks your pawn in the center, and nothing guards it.

steps.text: The second answer: guard it. Bring a piece or pawn that protects the pawn on e4.

also.d4c6: That works too: you trade knights first. This lesson guards the pawn.
also.f1b5: That leaves the pawn unguarded, but the game stays level: your bishop and quick castling make up for it. This lesson guards the pawn.

steps.hint: A knight, the queen or a pawn can each guard it.
steps.after: The pawn is guarded. If the knight takes it, you take the knight.

steps.text: The third answer: capture the attacker. Black's rook attacks your queen, and nothing guards the rook.
steps.hint: A pawn or the queen itself can take the rook.
steps.after: The attacker is gone, and you won a rook. Move it, guard it, or capture the attacker: ask before every move.

summary: Before every move, see what the last move attacks. Then move the piece, guard it, or capture the attacker.
